modern-new-technique-cuisine.verdict: Named teachers in most of the rooms, and now the Spanish ones too — a toolkit you can learn anywhere, beside the places that invented it

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes in five of the seven places, each a named living person: Martin Lippo at Vakuum in Barcelona, Éric Briffard at Le Cordon Bleu Paris, Miguel Ángel Cepeda in Puebla and Mexico City, Luis Arrufat with Txema Urda on the Basque Culinary Center's online course, and in Madrid the chefs Le Cordon Bleu names on its own Meet the Chefs page, read 17 September 2026 — Natalia Vázquez with David Vela, Manuel Lucas and Diego Muñoz. Girona's hotel school names nobody, and Sous Vide Australia now trains a venue's own team rather than the public. ⛔ Where we stand: EducatedTraveler ran a paid week with Martin Lippo in October 2026, so we are not a neutral party about him. Nobody pays to be on this map and no money reaches us from him; the way in without us is his own site, martinlippo.com.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open, and unusually so for the avant-garde. Private courses at Vakuum (his classroom courses for 2026 are sold out and no later date is shown, read 4 November 2026), four days in Paris with English translation as it is taught, a diplomado in Mexico, five weeks or an online course in San Sebastián, the avant-garde third of a nine-month diploma in Madrid, and a two-year professional course in Girona. Kitchen stages are not listed here: Arnaud's ruling of 4 November 2026 took them off the map, because you cannot book one. The hands can ruin it — a spherification bath and liquid nitrogen are unforgiving.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes, on the Paris course, the diplomado and the diplomas, which run as classes rather than as private hire. At Vakuum the way in is now a private course. The group size is published almost nowhere, and in a technique lab it decides whether you touch the equipment or watch it. Ask before you book.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes in Spain, and that is what changed. The toolkit travels — sous-vide was worked out at Troisgros in 1974 and belongs to every kitchen with a circulator — but Madrid Fusión has been the vanguard's own congress since 2003, and it meets in Madrid, which is now one of this craft's places. The places outside Spain are here for the toolkit; the ones inside it are here for the argument.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and no single body publishes a ladder: the qualification is a school's certificate, or in Madrid and Girona a diploma. What happens after the course is up to you and your own kitchen.

fermentation.verdict: One teacher you can name, in a room you can book, in Tokyo — and a single summer day in Copenhagen. Thin, and we would rather say so

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Yes in Tokyo: &LAB TOKYO's own page says Chie Ando teaches the course in person, and names her. In Copenhagen nobody is named — the summer day at noma Projects is taught by 'the noma team', and the Copenhagen distillery once listed here has moved to Brooklyn and runs no course.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Yes, two ways. &LAB TOKYO takes a stranger directly and arranges the dates when you apply; its three-day intensive is ¥156,000 before tax, taught in Japanese, with English support at ¥15,000 a day. noma Projects sells a ticket for 13 or 14 August 2027 to anyone who buys its yearly membership — a day, not a course.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Not reliably. &LAB's groups are one to four, so you may well be alone with the teacher, which is good teaching and no company. noma's summer day has a room full of people, for one day.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Not answered. Everything we have on both places comes from the people selling the course, and that cannot tell you whether the craft lives in the town around it.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been, and no body publishes a ladder for fermentation: a school's own certificate is the most there is.

fermentation.check: Graded from the two school pages, both read 4 November 2026. Nobody from EducatedTraveler has stood in either room. Every step of the Tokyo course is also sold online, which the school says itself.
fermentation.ceilingNote: Two places is too few to say more. A third with a named teacher and a date would change this grade before any visit would.

bread-and-boulangerie.verdict: Real doors, in English and in French, with dates and prices on them — and not one teacher we have yet named from a page we read

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Not yet, on our own reading. The École Internationale de Boulangerie names its founder, Thomas Teffri-Chambelland, but a founder is not a teacher. FERRANDI Paris and the École de Boulangerie et de Pâtisserie de Paris name nobody on the course pages we read on 4 November 2026. Ask who will be in the bakery with you.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Yes. FERRANDI Paris runs twelve weeks of bread and viennoiseries in English, 25 August to 19 November 2027, at €18,500. The École de Boulangerie et de Pâtisserie de Paris runs its CAP route from September, in French only and only for EU or Swiss nationals or holders of a work permit. In Copenhagen, Meyers Madhus sells one-day classes in English with dates on them. Le Cordon Bleu's Tokyo campus is closed for now.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: Yes. These are classes, not private lessons: the Paris CAP takes forty-eight a year in groups of twelve at the bench, and Meyers seats sixteen.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Not answered. Everything here comes from the schools themselves. A guild, a market or a bakers' competition would answer it, and we have not read one yet.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. The ladder exists in public — the CAP Boulanger is a state diploma with a published référentiel — and we have not adopted it on this page yet.

bread-and-boulangerie.check: Graded from the school pages read on 4 November 2026, not from a visit. Nobody from EducatedTraveler has stood in any of these bakeries. Viennoiserie was folded into this craft on 4 November 2026; its places are graded here with the rest.

new-basque-cuisine.verdict: A faculty the Basque chefs built for themselves, examined by a university rather than vouched for by a teacher — and the great names beside it are a lineage, not a class

conditions.n: Is there a teacher, and can we name them?
conditions.t: Lit, but not by the names you would expect, and the difference is the whole answer. The great kitchens here — Andoni Luis Aduriz's Mugaritz, Martín Berasategui's at Lasarte-Oria — offer a stage you apply for, not a course you book, and since 4 November 2026 this map does not list them as places to learn. The Basque Culinary Center, which is where a stranger can actually enrol, still names no teacher. What lights this answer is the other way in: its Culinary Techniques Mastery carries 6 ECTS awarded with Mondragon University, so somebody outside the kitchen sets the standard and marks against it. That is a weaker promise than a name and a stronger one than a brochure. Ask them who runs the five weeks; the names would be worth more than the credits.

conditions.n: Can a stranger get in, on a date you can book?
conditions.t: Open at the faculty. The Basque Culinary Center runs its Culinary Techniques Mastery at about 3,320 EUR and the Escuela de Cocina Luis Irizar a two-year professional specialisation. The restaurants take stagiaires on their own terms, which is why they are no longer on this map. Your hands can ruin it in either room.

conditions.n: Will there be other people learning beside you?
conditions.t: San Sebastián reads Legendary above, and the reason is not a school — it is that a town of a hundred and eighty thousand people holds one of the densest concentrations of serious kitchens in Europe, plus the faculty those kitchens founded. There is a generation above you here and one below, and they drink in the same bars.

conditions.n: Is the craft alive in this place, or is the school the only thing here?
conditions.t: Yes. San Sebastián Gastronomika fills the Kursaal in Donostia every autumn — 5–7 October in 2026 — a congress the city's own kitchens built and still fill. A town that hosts the argument about its cuisine is a town that cuisine belongs to. What we still have not done is walk the Gipuzkoa markets, which is where a week would teach more than the reading has.

conditions.n: Is there enough here to keep you learning for years?
conditions.t: Nobody of ours has been. The Basque Culinary Center's degree is awarded with Mondragon University, which is an outside body with an examination behind it — one of the better ladders on this map. We have read it. We have not seen anyone climb it.

new-basque-cuisine.ceilingNote: All five are reachable here: this cuisine belongs to its place, so one visit could answer the last one.
